newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Mixed Australian bonds outpace weak N.Z. debt.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Mixed Australian bonds outpace weak N.Z. debt.

text.p: A mixed perfromance by the Australian bond market saw it lag both U.S. and Canadian debt, but it outperformed weak New Zealand bonds, traders said.

Local bonds were tied up with the rollover in futures to December contracts from September positions ahead of their expiries on Monday, which tended to exaggerate price movements but boosted what would have been an otherwise a slim turnover.
However, N.Z. debt weakened sharply amid extreme disappointment over a bearish statement by the the RBNZ which saw no scope for an easing in policy before late 1997.
Forward projections of N.Z. inflation were stronger than expected -- peaking at 2.7 percent in September 1996 before falling to 2.1 percent in March 1997 and 0.8 percent in 1998.
The N.Z. market had been hoping for a more positive statement, which had seen it outperforming Australia at the start of the week.
New Zealand's 10-year bond yield premium over Australia now stands at around its highest level since going from a discount in July.
